notes.body:
ORCHESTRATOR CODE FIXES made while the plan is blocked on the locked workstation. Both are defects that directly caused failures found this round, and neither needs a screen.

1. scripts/mouse.ps1 - FIXED. It piped SetCursorPos's return value to Out-Null in all four call sites, so it printed 'moved to 960,300' and exited 0 while moving nothing. That false success masked the locked session for an entire take. Added an Assert-Moved helper that surfaces the boolean and exits 2 with a message naming the likely cause. Verified: it now exits 2 with 'SetCursorPos(960,300) failed - no input desktop. Is the workstation locked?' where it previously reported success. Note for anyone editing this file: it must stay pure ASCII. An em-dash written as UTF-8 ends in byte 0x94, which PowerShell reads under CP1252 as a closing curly quote and which silently breaks string parsing several lines later.

2. Two misleading comments corrected. lib/shots.mjs quoted the rounded cut times 85.1/86.0/87.0/88.1, and montage.mjs's own comment three lines above the correct code quoted 85.06/86.0/87.0/88.1. Both now carry the measured transcript times, and montage.mjs documents the real 0.15s lead-in defect.

DISCLOSURE: while syntax-checking I ran node -e with a dynamic import of montage.mjs, which executed the module and rebuilt assets/cursor/12-montage.mp4. That was careless. The rebuild used unchanged build logic so the output is equivalent, and it independently confirmed the 8.97s-against-9.21s shortfall, but the asset mtime moved and that is worth knowing when reasoning about staleness.

notes.author: orchestrator
notes.body:
MONTAGE TIMING DEFECT FIXED AND MEASURED. The fact-check failed 12-montage for cuts landing 0.15-0.17s early and for being 0.243s short of its slot. Its stated root cause - that the cut used the rounded times from the lib/shots.mjs comment - was wrong; montage.mjs line 41 already held the correct transcript values and the asset was built after that fix.

The real cause: WORDS is measured from shot.from, so WORDS[0] is 0.15, but the four stab pieces were concatenated starting at output-time 0.00 with nothing covering 0.00-0.15. That single gap shifted every cut early AND accounted for the shortfall - one defect the audit had counted as two. Fixed by having the first stab start at output-time 0 and reach 0.15s further back into its source.

Verified by scene detection on the rebuilt asset. Cuts now land at VO 86.277 / 87.043 / 88.077 / 89.177 against targets of 86.260 / 87.040 / 88.080 / 89.180 - inside half a frame on all four. Duration went from 8.967s to 9.133s against a 9.210s slot, cutting the held final frame from 0.243s to 0.077s, roughly two frames.

A WARNING FOR STEP 90 about the audit's instruction 9, which says to extend the montage tail past 9.25s so the reel never holds a still: DO NOT DO THAT. fitClip keeps a clip's TAIL, so a montage longer than its slot loses its HEAD, which would shift all four cuts late and undo the fix above. The correct target is exactly the slot length, and the residual 0.077s hold is already far inside the no-hold-over-one-second gate.

STILL OUTSTANDING on the montage, both blocked on the step 88 reshoots because they reference clip times in shots being re-filmed: instruction 7 (the 'write' stab currently plays over a frame where the ghost text is cleared and the lines are empty) and instruction 8 (the 'ship' stab plays over a crash callstack, which duplicates shot 11 and reads as failure rather than shipping; the audit suggests the p4 changelist from 06-conventions instead).

plans.summary: Define and prototype a lightweight Diagon Depot host where users can install team-built apps or scripts into their own account, apps communicate through governed contracts, and submissions pass automated and human safety review. The design will replace the unsafe idea of executing arbitrary code based only on inferred intent with explicit manifests, adapters, permissions, sandboxing, provenance, and revocation, while using AI analysis only as review assistance.

steps.title: Design the governed inter-app communication fabric
steps.context: Design how independently authored installed apps communicate without direct trust. Use a host-mediated message/event/data API with app identity attached, capability checks on publish/subscribe/request, versioned schemas, correlation IDs, timeouts, payload/size/rate limits, audit records, and failure isolation. Cover browser UI messaging, server/background work, user-scoped versus shared data, consent for sensitive data, discovery of compatible contracts, and backward-compatible evolution. Prevent direct database access and implicit global event access.
steps.acceptance_criteria: An ADR defines communication primitives, envelopes, authorization checks, schema registry/discovery, version negotiation, delivery guarantees, error semantics, observability, and at least three end-to-end interaction examples. Verification: contract fixtures validate, unauthorized publish/subscribe examples are denied, and cyclic or unavailable-app behavior is specified.
steps.carry_forward: Step 3 DONE. Delivered docs/secure-app-runtime/03-inter-app-communication-fabric.md (ADR) + schema/contract.schema.json + schema/validate-contract.mjs (zero-dep broker-simulating validator) + schema/contracts/examples/{valid-publish,valid-request,valid-subscribe}.json + schema/contracts/invalid/9 denial fixtures. Verified: validator self-test 0 unmet, npx prisma generate exit 0, npm run typecheck exit 0, additive-only (?? docs/secure-app-runtime/), package.json/lockfile untouched. KEY DECISIONS the downstream steps must honor: (1) Delivery = AT-MOST-ONCE for both events (best-effort fan-out, no durable queue) and requests (single outcome, NO auto-retry; events advisory, authoritative state via request/response). At-least-once (durable outbox + idempotency) forwarded as future work. (2) Broker DOES deep-validate payloads against declared contract schemas at the boundary, deny-by-default with code PAYLOAD_SCHEMA_INVALID; cheap checks (capability, allow-list, size) run BEFORE schema eval. (3) Auth pipeline order (guards confused-deputy R3): authenticate sender -> GRANTED (not requested) messaging.* -> DECLARED contract -> targets allow-list; unauthorized denied on authority before target existence leaks. (4) Failure isolation: not-installed/no-acceptor -> TARGET_UNAVAILABLE immediately; unresponsive -> TARGET_TIMEOUT + adapter Active->Suspended; caller always gets a typed error, never a hang/cascade. Cyclic: host-maintained callPath + hopDepth; re-entry -> CALL_CYCLE_DETECTED, depth>MAX_CALL_DEPTH(8) -> MAX_DEPTH_EXCEEDED. (5) HostSurface + GrantContext TS shapes defined in ADR section 10 as the SOLE authority path; all data user-scoped by default (R10); privileged caps need human grant + per-user consent. Error taxonomy in ADR section 8.3. Constants: envelope majors [1], MAX_CALL_DEPTH=8; reuses HOST_API_VERSION=1.3.0 from validate-manifest.mjs. FOR STEP 4 (submission review/sandboxing/runtime safety) the ADR section 14 hands off: (a) sandbox enforcement of postMessage/worker bridge (nonce + targetOrigin + CSP) proving no HostSurface bypass (R1); (b) contract review rubric = minimum required schema richness for accepted requests + reviewer surfacing of messaging.request allow-lists and emitted/accepted contracts; (c) adversarial test seeds for step 7 (forged sender, stale-issuedAt replay, allow-list bypass, oversized/mismatched payload, cycle/depth storms, crashed/hung target) mapped to section 8.3 codes; (d) wire broker rate-limiters to shared Redis before multi-replica (R7); (e) contract deprecation metadata drain from registry. steps.title: Design account installation and host-shell user experience
steps.context: Design the lightweight host experience inside Diagon Depot for each user account: discover an approved app, inspect permissions and publisher, install, grant or deny optional capabilities, launch embedded or external UI, see installed apps, connect compatible apps, manage defaults/data access, update, disable, uninstall, and recover from a quarantined app. Include clear trust indicators, capability-change re-consent, dependency conflicts, empty/error/loading states, accessibility, and administrator controls. Keep the shell usable when one app crashes or is unavailable.
steps.acceptance_criteria: User journeys and wire-level interaction specification cover install, first launch, app-to-app connection, permission change, update, disable/quarantine, and uninstall; each state identifies user/admin actions and safety messaging. Verification: acceptance walkthroughs can be followed without hidden steps and map every screen/action to host APIs from prior designs.
steps.carry_forward: Step 5 DONE. Delivered docs/secure-app-runtime/05-account-installation-host-shell-ux.md plus machine-checkable backing: ux/host-api-surface.json (closed registry of every step-2/3/4 lifecycle state, HostSurface/AppAdapter member, capability id, error code, existing+proposed ActivityLog action), ux/screens.json, ux/flows/01-install..07-uninstall.json (56 steps, 7 required journeys), ux/check-flows.mjs (zero-dep validator). Verified: checker OK (0 unmet across 56 steps/7 journeys), npm run typecheck exit 0 on Node v24.14.0, git diff --check clean, additive-only (?? docs/secure-app-runtime/). KEY DECISIONS step 6 (implement vertical slice) must honor: (1) New top-level flag-gated nav entry '/my-apps' (mirrors the existing showAssets precedent in lib/site-nav.ts), NOT a Browse-sidebar facet like My Tools -- it's an operating mode (mounted surface + permission controls + kill switch), not a browse facet. (2) The existing desktop InstallButton/InstallWizard (native download+run) is UNTOUCHED and stays visually/label-distinct from the new account-scoped install ('Install locally' vs 'Install to my account') -- never merge these into one button. (3) Grant review UI shows Requested/Approved/Granted as three ALWAYS-DISTINCT states, never one checkbox; privileged capabilities (host.identity.email, net.fetch, catalog.write) are always default-OFF with a forced separate consent step, both at install and at first runtime use. (4) 'Quarantined' is a UX-ONLY label over the existing step-2 Suspended state with reason=security, vs plain amber Suspended for reason=health -- step 6 must add a `reason` column/field to the Installation's suspension metadata, NEVER a 5th lifecycle state; Quarantined has no self-service re-enable (only a fresh-review'd digest can clear it, step4 §6.5). (5) Dependency-conflict warning (Connections tab computes dependents from the broker's contracts.accepts allow-list registrations) must block-with-acknowledgment before disable/uninstall of an app others call, to avoid surprise TARGET_UNAVAILABLE cascades. (6) Proposed API surface (route-per-action, mirrors app/api/promotions/**): POST/GET /api/installations, POST .../enable, POST .../disable, DELETE ..., PATCH .../grants, POST .../consent, POST .../update, GET .../connections, GET .../activity, POST /api/admin/app-runtime/revoke. (7) Proposed additive ActivityAction ids for lib/activity/actions.ts: APP_INSTALLED, APP_ENABLED, APP_DISABLED, APP_SUSPENDED, APP_QUARANTINED, APP_REVOKED, APP_UNINSTALLED, APP_GRANT_CHANGED, APP_CONSENT_RECORDED, APP_UPDATED, APP_HEALTH_RECOVERED (alongside step3's APP_MSG_* set) -- wire these into the existing generic ActivityLogPanel, don't fork a new audit UI. (8) Reuse, don't fork: lib/use-focus-trap.ts + the InstallWizard dialog pattern, components/StatusBadge.tsx tone tokens, components/toast/ToastProvider.tsx, components/admin/AdminConsole.tsx's tabbed-section pattern (add an 'App Runtime' tab there, don't build a separate admin surface) -- a new visual language would undercut the 'same trusted host' message the UX is built around. (9) Data model precedent: an `Installation` table modeled on UserAppLocation ([userId,key] unique), additive migration, APPS_RUNTIME_ENABLED flag off by default (same pattern as DEPOT_SYNC_ENABLED/ASSETS_FEATURE_ENABLED). (10) Step 1's recommended thin vertical slice (§7: one adapter, e.g. worker-script or static-microfrontend) is enough to exercise every screen in the step-5 doc once; remote-web-app and the fuller cross-app Connections scenario can follow. FOR STEP 7 (verification): adversarial UI tests forwarded -- prove a hidden/disabled install action for an unapproved tool can't be clicked past; prove an unapproved capability can't be toggled on via direct API calls even if a client bypasses the dialog (server must independently re-reject with UNDECLARED_CAPABILITY/TARGET_NOT_ALLOWED, not just hide the control); prove the dependency-conflict warning actually prevents/warns on silent breakage in an end-to-end test with two installed fixture apps (reuses step3's Render Dashboard/USD Linter/Shot Builder fixture cast). BRIDGE TIP (unchanged from prior steps): call the plan-ledger CLI with `--input-file <path-to-json>` on Windows/PowerShell rather than `--input '<json>'` -- PowerShell strips/mangles embedded double quotes in single-quoted args even with `--%`; a temp JSON file avoids the whole class of escaping bugs. Docs-only verify command: fnm env --shell power-shell | Out-String | Invoke-Expression; fnm use default; npm run typecheck; node docs/secure-app-runtime/ux/check-flows.mjs. Working repo = C:\Users\Jose.Abraham\dd-secure-app-runtime (ava-diagon-depot, branch feat/secure-app-runtime).

notes.body: Review round 3 functional corrections: 1) HostedAppInstallation currently stores only appKey/approved:boolean manifest and has no ToolVersion/ReleaseAsset/hash evidence. steps.title: Implement evidence, provenance, and confidence guardrails
steps.context: Inside the rooted workspace, define the epistemic and ease-of-use contract used by every interaction, analysis, and generated artifact. Do not claim that hallucinations can be eliminated absolutely. Require claims to distinguish observed facts, computed results, assumptions, and recommendations; cite source file/sheet/range or Atlassian item where possible; report a numeric confidence percentage and concise basis whenever confidence is below 100%; say unknown when evidence is absent; prohibit invented citations, fabricated calculations, and silent inference. Also establish ease for the end user as a standing design direction: prefer plain language, safe defaults, guided choices, discoverable commands, actionable errors, and minimal setup over exposing implementation details. Implement this as project Cursor rules plus reusable response and claim-ledger templates, with machine-checkable examples and tests.

steps.title: Establish the spreadsheet support contract and regression matrix

Define exactly which behaviors are supported, rejected with actionable errors, or intentionally preserved only in the untouched source. Do not claim general Excel compatibility from CSV-only tests.

notes.author: orchestrator
notes.body:
Orchestrator review round 1 corrections, grounded in code:
1. Identity contract drift: adapters.ts builds p4://<depot>, confluence://<host>/pages/<id>, jira://<host>/issues/<id>. RFC requires configured non-secret aliases and exact p4://<server-id>/<depot-path>, confluence://<site-id>/page/<id>, jira://<site-id>/issue/<immutable-id>. Require/validate p4 server alias in connector env/config and Atlassian siteId in source config; use exact singular paths; update fixtures and stable-ID tests. Never derive identity from mutable URL host.
2. Tombstones: source-sync.ts tombstones every item absent from one complete list. Implement two-successive-complete-scan confirmation for Confluence/Jira using persisted sourceCursor pendingMissing IDs. First miss retains cloned current membership and records pending; second consecutive miss emits tombstone. Explicit authoritative 404/deletion may tombstone immediately. Cursor must not advance on partial/failure.
3. Diagon current coverage: worker sourceEvents reads ReleaseAsset rows from every APPROVED version and omits ToolVersion.zipPath. For each tool choose exactly current website version (PROMOTED preferred, else latest APPROVED by deterministic createdAt/id); ingest its source ZIP as diagon://tool-version/<version-id>/source plus all its ReleaseAssets. A new EAV/tool version must tombstone old current files in the new generation while immutable versions stay archived.
4. Automatic mutation trigger: add a default-off helper that durably enqueues enabled diagon-files source reconciliation after relevant upload/status APPROVED/PROMOTED/withdraw/delete transitions (tool-upload, status route, promotion result). Upload/status success must not be rolled back by indexing; enqueue failure must create/update visible retryable job state and tagged log. Scheduled full reconciliation remains the repair sweep. Add tests.
5. Immutable object archive: no code currently writes rawArchiveKey/normalizedArchiveKey or calls writeStored. Before DB staging, write available normalized text and available raw bytes to content-addressed DIAGON_RAG_ARCHIVE_PREFIX keys via storage, no semantic overwrite; set archive keys on events. Exact replay must reuse keys. Add dependency-injected tests. If raw bytes are unavailable, record normalized only honestly.
6. Retry/DLQ bug: processRagQueueMessage catch sets status FAILED retryable=true; next delivery claimJob cannot claim FAILED, returns busy, and runRagWorker deletes any non-throwing busy message. Fix so retryable failures remain reclaimable and busy/in-flight messages are never deleted. Delete only processed/already-terminal. Request ApproximateReceiveCount; at configured max record DEAD_LETTERED/terminal evidence before allowing SQS redrive. Add tests for first failure, redelivery success, busy non-delete, and terminal delete.
7. Intake enqueue failure must persist failureCode/message/retryable on the durable job before returning 5xx, without secrets.
8. Re-run focused/full tests, worker bundle, typecheck/lint/build/Prisma/contracts/diff. Report exact counts and limitations. No live external calls, Docker, ledger mutation, commit, push, or deploy.

steps.title: Establish the authoritative SceneRig authoring recipe from the real toolsets
steps.context:
Repo: C:\Users\Jose.Abraham\Documents\cursor-showcase. Unreal Editor is running (PID confirmed, responsive) and its MCP server is bound at http://127.0.0.1:8000/mcp from inside the editor.

HOW TO REACH UNREAL. There is no .cursor/mcp.json in this repo, so you do NOT have Unreal MCP tools. Use the repo's own client, lib/unreal.mjs, from a node script: import { connect, callToolset, describeToolset, listTools } from './lib/unreal.mjs', call connect() first (the plugin enforces initialize + notifications/initialized), then callToolset(toolsetName, toolName, args). Epic gates the real tools behind a call_tool meta-tool, which callToolset already wraps. Working examples: scripts/rig-probe.mjs, scripts/rig-schema.mjs, scripts/rig-skills.mjs, scripts/rig-classes.mjs, scripts/rig-replay.mjs.

READ FIRST, IN THIS ORDER.
1. C:\Users\Jose.Abraham\Downloads\scenerig-authoring\scenerig-authoring.mdc ??? the user supplied this and asked that we study SceneRig properly rather than guess.
2. The two UAgentSkills it points at, fetched live via ToolsetRegistry.AgentSkillToolset.GetSkills: SceneRigAuthoringSkill (the outline-first loop, the event timing model, the handoff to ObjectTools for per-action properties) and SceneRigStandardLayoutSkill (the canonical root layout plus worked recipes for fades, per-cut shots, and adding a character). The .mdc is explicit that the tool schemas carry argument shapes but the CONVENTIONS live in these two skills. Fetch both before concluding anything.

RULES THE .mdc STATES THAT THE RECIPE MUST CARRY FORWARD.
- Two toolsets cover authoring: SceneRigEditor.SceneRigToolset for generic structure, timing, proxies, timeline layers and editor refresh; SundanceEditor.SundanceSceneRigToolset for the canonical Sundance layout, StandardizeSceneRig and character lookup. Do not hand-roll SR edits with generic ObjectTools property pokes.
- Prefer StandardizeSceneRig over hand-authoring. It applies the whole canonical layout in one idempotent single-undo pass, and it will not invent content ??? so the shape of a task is: add content with the primitives, then Standardize to settle the layout.
- Never make a new SR by duplicating an existing one. Use SundanceSceneRigToolset.CreateSceneRig with a class from SceneRigToolset.ListSceneRigClasses. A duplicate inherits the source's preview level and preview bookmark.
- For a fixed duration use Self, not Relative aimed at your own Start. A 30-frame fade is SelfRelative(1.0).
- Never guess an action's property names. Hundreds of USceneAction_* classes have unrelated property sets and a wrong name fails SILENTLY rather than erroring. Always ObjectTools.list_properties on the element the toolset handed back before set_properties.

WHAT THIS STEP MUST SETTLE IN WRITING, so the capture step never guesses.
1. The exact call sequence from nothing to a standardized three-character cinematic rig with an active camera, naming the owning toolset and method for every call.
2. Which properties actually place an actor in the preview world. Known from prior work on this machine, but confirm against the skills and against live list_properties output: SceneAction_Transform defaults to transformMode 'RootConstraint', which means an authored relativeTransform does NOT drive placement; transformMode 'SetActorTransform' with bForceTransform true is what worked. Visibility is SceneAction_Visibility.shouldBeHidden, which must be false for the proxy to render. Reconcile this against what the skills say is the sanctioned way ??? if the skills prescribe a different mechanism for staging a character, prefer theirs and say why.
3. Reading results reliably. MCP replies wrap payloads: unwrap with value?.returnValue ?? value before indexing, and value?.element ?? value when a call returns an element handle. A prior run threw 'TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 0)' because GetSceneRigOutline's result was indexed without unwrapping returnValue.
4. Locating a cast member's Transform action deterministically. Fuzzy name matching failed before with 'Error: Missing Transform action for NatsaiOnai'. FindElements with an explicit elementClass refPath of /Script/SceneRig.SceneAction_Transform plus an empty nameSubstring, then matching on parent.refPath, is what worked.
5. Safe teardown. Do NOT call AssetTools.delete on an open SceneRig_Cinematic: it enters ObjectTools::ForceDeleteObjects and crashed this editor while FSlowTask rebuilt text after the SceneRig preview world was torn down. scripts/rig-clean.mjs already skips it; the recipe must record why.
6. Staging geometry for camera: world-space translations and yaws putting three characters clearly apart and mutually visible from one camera proxy, plus which viewport control frames them. The SceneRig editor exposes 'Move View to Scene Root' and a focus binding, and there is a Game Preview viewport tab.

Read-only in the editor where you can be. You may create a scratch rig to introspect if that is the only way to get real list_properties output, but put it in /Game/CursorDemo, never save it, and do not delete it with AssetTools.delete.

Do not modify any capture or build script in this step. Research and write only. Where a claim comes from live MCP output rather than the .mdc or the skills, quote the actual call and the actual response.

steps.layman: The researcher figured out why the SceneRig demo kept failing, and it was three separate causes, none of them the one we assumed. The editor needs a specific plain refresh call to actually spawn characters into the viewport, and we had been using a variant that skips that. The characters were lined up on the same axis as the camera so one hid behind the other, which is the overlap that kept getting rejected. And when a command to Unreal fails it quietly returns a text message instead of erroring, so the old scripts were sailing straight past their own failures. All three are now written down as a step-by-step recipe with real coordinates.

Four findings explain all three prior SceneRig failures. (1) Rejected MCP calls do NOT throw - they resolve with an ordinary payload containing a message like 'input param filter is required' and the process exits 0, so indexing the result yields undefined later. INDEPENDENT EVIDENCE THAT THE EXISTING CAPTURE IS INADEQUATE ??? recapture, do not reuse. The refactor-surgeon sampled frames from out/rig/real-scenerig-authoring.mp4 while auditing shot provenance and found: at 1.5s the viewport shows sky/desert with a transform gizmo and an effectively empty outliner; the segment build09 pulls at -ss 3.2 lands on a modal 'Spawning Actors' progress dialog. This is a second, independent confirmation on top of the user's own rejection, so the five must-show beats in this step's context are not satisfiable by re-editing the existing clip. Produce out/rig/scenerig-authoring-final.mp4 from a fresh take.
READ docs/scenerig-recipe.md FIRST - it is a 15-step executable sequence and it supersedes the assumptions in your step context. Four findings from step 84, each verified by the orchestrator against raw captures in out/probe/, change how you must work:

1. FAILED MCP CALLS DO NOT THROW. They resolve with an ordinary payload containing a message like 'Function "ListCharacterIDs", input param "filter" is required', and the process exits 0. Indexing that result gives you undefined several lines later. This - not the returnValue unwrap - is the real origin of the 'TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 0)' from the earlier attempt. Use the assertOk helper the recipe mandates on EVERY call. Do not assume a call succeeded because nothing threw.

2. PROPERTY-SETTING IS NOT WHAT MAKES A CHARACTER APPEAR. SceneRigAuthoringSkill states, verbatim from the live payload: 'The incremental path rebuilds the outliner but does not respawn actors, so the new proxy stays unresolved and shows red in the tree with nothing in the viewport. The bare call is what makes a character actually appear.' So after adding a proxy actor or changing a binding, call RefreshSceneRigEditor BARE - omit elementToSelect. Every earlier empty-viewport failure was this, not transformMode and not shouldBeHidden.

3. THE OVERLAP WAS GEOMETRY, NOT A FAILED TRANSFORM. The live rig has the camera at {x:-900,y:0,z:220} yaw 0 looking down +X, with characters at {x:-260,y:0,z:0} and {x:260,y:0,z:0}. All three are collinear on X, so the second actor sits directly behind the first. The transforms were applying correctly the whole time - worldTransform matched relativeTransform. Use the recipe's Y-spread coordinates, which are shown to land the three characters at 704/960/1216 px across a 1920-wide frame and to survive a horizontal FOV from 90 degrees down to about 40.

4. ORDER IS FORCED. SceneRigStandardLayoutSkill says Standardize OWNS the per-character Transform track, so you cannot find that Transform before Standardize runs. Sequence is: add cast, Standardize, THEN place. This is why the earlier run threw 'Missing Transform action for NatsaiOnai'.

HONESTLY UNVERIFIED, handle empirically rather than assuming: whether transformMode defaults to RootConstraint (immaterial - set it explicitly regardless); whether Standardize creates the camera action unprompted (recipe step 11 handles it conditionally); and the 'Move View to Scene Root' / 'Game Preview' viewport affordances, which a depth-30 Slate snapshot did not expose - you will need to establish framing empirically with scripts/mouse.ps1 and SlateInspectorToolset, and the SceneRig editor is its own 1920x1080 window (Slate id w20).

A scratch rig from a prior run may still be open in /Game/CursorDemo. Note also that the live proxies carry bForceTransform false, so do not assume prior runs left the state you expect - read values back before relying on them.
UNBLOCK PROCEDURE. Requires the user: unlock the Windows console session and leave it unlocked (do not lock it again while the take runs). Then a single command shoots it:

    node scripts/rig86-take.mjs

That script already implements the full 15-step recipe with assertOk on every call, the forced cast-then-Standardize-then-place order, and a recorder stopped by the build completing rather than a guessed -t. It hard-gates on input-desktop availability and exits 2 rather than emitting a black file, so it is safe to run blind.

STAGING IS ALREADY FIXED AND PERSISTED in the live rig - do not redo it: NatsaiOnai {x:0,y:-240,z:0} yaw 160, PoppySweeting {x:140,y:0,z:0} yaw 180, SebastianSallow {x:0,y:240,z:0} yaw -160, camera {x:-900,y:0,z:170} yaw 0. Verified via worldTransform==relativeTransform, projecting to 704/960/1216 px with 256 px gaps.

STILL UNRESOLVED, resolve it first thing once unlocked: post-restage the SceneRig preview viewport read as empty grey sky, and a locked session cannot distinguish 'preview world genuinely empty' from 'Slate not repainting an occluded window'. Must-show requirement 3 (three characters visibly apart in the preview viewport) depends entirely on which it is. Check this before recording a full take.

DO NOT TRUST scripts/mouse.ps1 as written - it pipes SetCursorPos's return to Out-Null and prints success while doing nothing. Fix it to surface the boolean before relying on it for framing.

The reason it kept coming out empty had nothing to do with the characters or their positions - the editor just opens with the wrong panel in front, a black one, and every previous recording filmed that instead of the panel where you can actually see the scene. Once the right tab is clicked, everything that was supposedly broken turns out to have been working all along. There was a second, separate problem where two of the three characters stood in a line and hid each other from this particular angle, which is now fixed by spreading them apart in two directions instead of one. The audit measured the defect correctly - all four cuts 0.15-0.17s early - but attributed it to 'whoever cut it used the rounded times in the lib/shots.mjs comment'. THE REAL CAUSE, found by reading the build loop: WORDS is measured from shot.from, so WORDS[0] = 85.06 - 84.91 = 0.15. But the four stab pieces are concatenated starting at output-time 0.00 with nothing covering 0.00-0.15. The entire montage is therefore shifted 0.15s early, and the clip finishes short by the same amount. This predicts exactly the 0.15s the audit measured, and it explains the separate '0.243s short, last frame held' row in the audit's own clock table - those are one defect, not two. Rebuilding montage.mjs unchanged reproduces 8.97s against the 9.21s slot.

The fix needs a lead-in piece covering 0.00-0.15, which is a creative call: either the first stab is already mid-shot when the montage opens, or the cut onto 'understand' is sacrificed. Left for step 90 to decide rather than guessed at here. The two misleading comments have been corrected in place.

steps.title: Quality gate all three videos on sync, motion, legibility and duration
steps.context:

This is the planner's quality gate made executable. The user's bar is 'most impressive footage of cursor capability you can, hits the right facts and visually appealing' and 'all of your best quality that sync to the audio and can be displayed'. Nothing ships that fails a check here.

Run every check against all three videos:
1. Container and stream conformance. 1920x1080, exactly 30fps with no variable frame rate, h264 high profile, yuv420p, aac audio at a consistent sample rate. Reject anything with a 0/0 frame rate on the audio stream or a mismatched SAR.
2. Motion. scripts/motion.mjs already exists to detect held frames; run it on each video and confirm no hold exceeds one second. Report the longest hold and where it is.
3. Audio sync. For each video, cross-correlate the muxed audio against the corresponding span of assets/vo/CURSOR_VO_3.wav and report the offset in milliseconds. Anything over one frame, 33.3ms, fails.
4. Word-to-picture alignment. Spot-check the six load-bearing moments and confirm the picture is present by the time the word is spoken: Tab ghost text before 20.4s, Ctrl+K diff before 22.2s, p4 output before 42.46s, Unreal MCP answer inside 53.58-65.30, crash triage before 77.98s, montage cuts at 85.06, 86.26, 87.04, 88.08. 6. Banned content. No castle frame anywhere. No composed or synthetic Unreal or SceneRig UI anywhere. No overlapping character proxies in any SceneRig frame. Confirm each by citing stills.
7. No black frames, no dropped frames at cut points, no audio clicks at the splices in B and C.

steps.title: Write the stage aesthetic doctrine that makes a build look deliberate
steps.context:
Write the checkable aesthetic doctrine that makes an MCP-built stage look deliberate rather than randomly scattered. This is the 'well thought out' half of the request. A separate step covers the mechanical MCP half, so stay out of tool syntax entirely here.

Target: a set/environment built live in an Unreal 5.8 level for an on-camera demo. It has to read as composed within a few seconds on screen, at normal playback speed, to a viewer who is not an artist.

Cover these six areas, and make every point checkable rather than vibes:
1. Staging and blocking: a single clear focal point, foreground/midground/background layering, depth cues, negative space, leading lines, avoiding tangents, and avoiding evenly-spaced 'sprinkled prop' syndrome.
2. Scale and human reference: how to keep proportions legible and why a human-scale object belongs in frame.
3. Lighting design: key/fill/rim as an intentional ratio, motivated practicals, colour-temperature contrast between key and ambient, value structure so the focal point is the brightest or darkest thing in frame, and why flat uniform ambient kills a shot.
4. Materials and colour: a limited palette with one dominant and one accent, varied roughness so highlights read, and avoiding pure white or pure black albedo.
5. Atmosphere: fog and volumetrics used to separate depth planes, plus exposure and bloom restraint.
6. Camera language: lens choice and what a focal length communicates, eye height, headroom, rule of thirds, and specifically what makes a REVEAL move feel motivated rather than an aimless drifting flythrough.

For each area give a small number of named defaults, numeric wherever possible, that a machine can apply without taste (for example a key-to-fill ratio, a fog density starting point, a focal length default for a wide establishing reveal). Pair every default with the failure mode it prevents, because the failure mode is what makes the default arguable rather than arbitrary.

Also define a short 'the stage looks wrong' triage list mapping a visual symptom to its likely cause (for example 'everything looks flat' maps to fill too close to key plus no rim plus no fog).

Write to D:/sun-dev/.cursor/skills/build-unreal-stage/reference/stage-doctrine.md. Checked-in deliverable: ASCII only, no em-dashes, en-dashes, curly quotes or ellipsis characters. Tight prose, no filler. Do not run any p4 command.

Every area supplies at least one concrete default a machine can apply without judgement, each paired with the failure mode it prevents. Includes a symptom-to-cause triage list of at least six entries. Verified ASCII-only with no smart punctuation. Contains no Unreal tool names or MCP call syntax, since that belongs to the workflow rule. No p4 commands were run.

All six areas covered, 61 numeric defaults, 15 triage entries, 10-item final gate. Load-bearing defaults include hero at 15-25 percent of frame area beating the runner-up 2.5:1, three depth bands separated by 15 percent luminance, key-to-fill 6:1 with a 1500 K warm/cool split, and a 24 mm reveal gated on parallax (foreground occluder traverses 25 percent of frame width while background moves 5 percent or less). The strongest idea is that a reveal requires prior concealment, so the start frame must hide 80 percent of the hero and an occluder must clear during the first 40 percent of the move; that is what separates a reveal from a drift. Contains no Unreal or MCP tool references, as required.

steps.context:
Write D:/sun-dev/.cursor/rules/unreal-stage-mcp-workflow.mdc, the rule that tells an agent HOW to drive the Unreal MCP to build a stage safely and fast during a live demo.

Source material, both written in earlier steps: D:/sun-dev/.cursor/skills/build-unreal-stage/reference/mcp-surface.md (verified tool inventory) and reference/camera-rail.md (verified spline camera recipe). Every tool name in this rule must come from those two files. Inventing a tool name is the specific failure this rule exists to prevent, so do not add one from memory.

Cover these eight areas:
1. Mandatory order of operations: run .cursor/skills/check-unreal-editor before anything, and check list_toolsets plus the AgentSkillToolset ListSkills/GetSkills before deep problem solving. The existing rule .cursor/rules/unreal-mcp-skills.mdc already mandates the skills check, so DEFER to it and cite it rather than duplicating it.
2. Asset discovery through SemanticSearch instead of guessing /Game paths, and what to do when nothing suitable exists.
3. The ObjectTools list_properties-before-set_properties requirement, since property names vary per class and cannot be guessed. Skipping it causes silent failures.

5. Outliner folder and actor-label naming, so the result is legible on camera and trivially deletable.

steps.carry_forward:
CRITICAL FINDINGS FROM STEP 94 - these OVERRIDE assumptions baked into your step context. Full detail and verbatim evidence in reference/mcp-surface.md.

1. SEMANTIC SEARCH IS BROKEN. SemanticSearchToolset.Search fails in this editor with 'Embedding generation failed: HTTP 401: Not authenticated'. Do NOT write a rule that mandates Search. The VERIFIED discovery recipe is: AssetTools.find_assets (folder_path AND name both required, '' = whole project; substring, unranked, no result cap) to get a seed path, then SemanticSearchToolset.FindSimilar on that seed to expand semantically and read the indexed captions. Say plainly that Search is currently broken so nobody rediscovers it live on camera.

2. THERE IS NO VERIFIED UNDO. No undo tool exists in any of the 60 toolsets. The 'one execute_tool_script equals one undo step' claim appears ONLY in the SceneRigToolset description and was NOT empirically tested. The non-destructive posture must therefore rest on three things: a dedicated outliner folder, explicit teardown by deleting that folder's actors, and never saving the level. Do NOT tell the agent to rely on Ctrl+Z or on ProgrammaticToolset for undo. You may still recommend ProgrammaticToolset for batching (fewer round trips), just not for undo.

3. ObjectTools.set_properties takes `values` as a JSON-FORMATTED STRING, not an object. list_properties and get_properties return strings too. This silently misbehaves if you pass an object.

4. LogsToolset.GetLogEntries defaults `category` to 'LogsToolset', so omitting it filters the log to the toolset's own chatter and you wrongly conclude your action never ran. Always pass category explicitly.

5. ActorTools has NO actor-to-actor attach. Hierarchy must be set AT SPAWN via the `parent` argument of SceneTools.add_to_scene_from_asset / add_to_scene_from_class.

6. Every actor/asset/class/component argument is an object {"refPath": "..."}, never a bare path string, and tools return the same shape. Pass returned refs straight back in.

7. call_tool takes tool_name WITHOUT the toolset prefix; toolset_name carries the prefix.

8. EditorAppToolset advertises console variables but only ships SearchCVars.

9. The MCP server id is `unreal-mcp` from a headless CLI session, but `user-unreal-mcp` inside the Cursor app. Mention both so the rule works from either surface.

10. CaptureViewport was described but NOT invoked in step 94, so the image round-trip was untested there. Step 96 exercises it for real - READ reference/camera-rail.md before you write the screenshot-verification section, and use whatever it proves.


=== CRITICAL FINDINGS FROM STEP 96 (reference/camera-rail.md, 580 lines) ===
All nine were hit for real in the live editor and all have proven workarounds. Do NOT restate the recipe in your rule - point at reference/camera-rail.md. But DO surface the traps below, because they are the ones that burn demo time.

11. SPLINE WRITES DO NOT TAKE EFFECT. USplineComponent has no PostEditChangeProperty override, so writing spline points via MCP never calls UpdateSpline(). The reparam table stays stale, GetSplineLength() returns only the first segment, and the camera mount crawls along one segment instead of the whole path. The recipe bakes Catmull-Rom tangents and an arc-length reparam table by hand. Flag this as the single biggest trap.

12. TWO-PHASE ARRAY WRITES. ObjectTools.set_properties cannot resize an array and change its element values in one call ('insertion points are ambiguous'). Every array write is two calls: resize first with existing elements sent back byte-identical, then set values.

13. SequencerTools.set_camera_cut_binding IS BROKEN server-side: 'call() takes at most 0 arguments (1 given)'. Workaround: ObjectTools.set_properties on the MovieSceneCameraCutSection CameraBindingID with the camera binding guid, sequenceId 0, resolveParentIndex 0.

14. bake_channel_keys returns a single value rather than a per-frame curve (likely display-frame vs tick-frame mismatch), so it cannot verify easing. Verify by driving set_playhead_frame + force_evaluate and reading the property back.

15. CaptureViewport via execute_tool_script needs an explicit all-zero annotations object or it errors with 'input param annotations needs a default value'. THIS IS THE VERIFIED SCREENSHOT PATH - step 94 could not confirm it, step 96 did. Use it for the verify-by-screenshot section.

16. AssetTools.write_file only allows .csv .html .json .md .py .txt. Write base64 to .txt and decode to .png separately.

17. SequencerTools.remove_section requires BOTH track and section refs.

18. The rail's PreviewMesh_Mount sits exactly on the cine camera lens and obscures every capture. Set bShowRailVisualization=false before capturing. This ruined the first capture set.

19. AIMING: do NOT use ActorTools.look_at or CineCameraActor LookatTrackingSettings. Both depend on actor ticking that does not reliably occur in-editor outside PIE. Use bLockOrientationToRail=true on a circular spline centred on the hero, plus a constant relative yaw offset on the camera - pure transform hierarchy, no ticking dependency. Measured yaw error 1.35 degrees worst case.

20. THE EDITOR DOES NOT TICK IN THE BACKGROUND. Sequencer-driven property writes do not propagate on idle scrub. Anything that needs to move for a screenshot must be driven through the synchronous property path. This is a general constraint, not a camera-only one.

21. TEARDOWN REALITY: step 96 restored the level to its original 36 actors and deleted its temp asset, but the level DIRTY FLAG is still set and cannot be cleared. Your teardown section must say plainly: never save, and expect the editor to offer a save prompt on close - discarding is the correct answer.

steps.title: Fold validation findings back in and stage a Perforce changelist
steps.context:
Close the loop: fix everything the validation run found, then put the deliverables in a Perforce changelist for the user to review.

Input: D:/sun-dev/.cursor/skills/build-unreal-stage/reference/validation-run.md holds a numbered defect list, each entry naming a file and section. Work the list in order. Files in scope: .cursor/rules/unreal-stage-composition.mdc, .cursor/rules/unreal-stage-mcp-workflow.mdc, .cursor/skills/build-unreal-stage/SKILL.md, .cursor/skills/build-unreal-stage/prompt.md, and .cursor/skills/build-unreal-stage/reference/*.md. If a defect is a genuine product decision rather than a bug, leave it and say so explicitly rather than guessing at what the user wants.

Perforce: this workspace is Helix Core, not git. D:/sun-dev/.p4ignore.txt ignores .cursor/* but explicitly un-ignores .cursor/rules/**, .cursor/skills/** and .cursor/permissions.json, so these files are meant to be submitted. Create a DEDICATED pending changelist with a description and never leave anything in the default changelist: run `p4 change -o`, set a tab-indented Description, pipe it back through `p4 change -i`, then `p4 add -c <NUM> <file>` for each new file and `p4 edit -c <NUM> <file>` for any existing file you modified. Never clear a read-only flag by hand. Verify with `p4 opened -c <NUM>` and confirm `p4 opened -c default` is clean. Do NOT submit; leave the changelist pending for the user.

Filetype note: on this server every new text file is added as text+C. That is a storage-compression modifier, is expected and harmless, and is not an encoding problem. Do not try to reopen it as plain text and do not report it as an issue.

Before opening the changelist, verify every deliverable is ASCII-only with no em-dashes, en-dashes, curly quotes or ellipsis characters, since a single non-ASCII byte makes Perforce treat the file as Unicode and breaks the build.

Finally, re-read the two rules end to end as a fresh reader and cut anything that is now redundant, contradicted by the validation run, or simply padding.

Nothing was submitted. The changelist description names the change and its purpose. A final read-through pass was done and any cuts are noted in the report.
